decisions_made: CS5's safe pair is X={t,4}, Y={b}, confirmed against Theorem 5.2's exact side conditions (page 14): X subset {d,t,4}, Y subset {d,b,5} are disjoint domains; 't in X and 5 in Y implies b in Y' is vacuous (5 not in Y); 'b in Y implies 4 in X' holds. Only tR/tL/fourR/fourL/bStruct are landed -- d^[], t^[], 4^[], 5^[] (Figure 4) and the naive eq.(3.2)/(3.3) b-rules are out of scope for this instance.

4-degree/4-input (fourR/fourL) are genuinely distinct rules from NCK's own diamond-output/box-input (diaR/boxL, Phase 9), not duplicates: Figure 2's rules build the modal formula fresh from a bare leaf, Figure 3's 4-rules reposition an already-formed modal formula out of a shared box -- confirmed by re-rendering page 6 and comparing premises directly.

bStruct's sigma/Delta are generic NestedLhs, not Proposition: Figure 4 is genuinely structural (no polarity marker in the source), unlike Figure 2/3's formula-building rules. Spelled lowercase sigma, not capital Sigma: Mathlib binds capital Sigma as sigma-type binder notation, unusable as a plain identifier -- same clash class as Pi/pi documented in Context.lean (Phase 7).

NestedProof.mono is landed as the index-equality transport precursor (Eq-cast, height-preserving hence non-increasing), not yet Figure (3.1)'s full content-weakening admissible rule -- the plan's own Phase 19 explicitly says its first task is to 'extend Phase 10's .mono to the height-preserving statement', confirming this is the intended narrower scope for this phase's 2.5-hour budget, not a premature attempt at the 18-constructor admissibility induction. Documented as an inline plan-file annotation, not a silent substitution.
